rejected.title: Tourism and health
card: Tourism is travel to other places for leisure or business. It is one of the world's largest industries, and it affects the health of people living in the places visitors go to.
Benefits
Tourism brings income and jobs. Through wages and taxes, it can help fund better housing, food, sanitation, schools and health care.
Risks
Travellers can carry infectious diseases, such as measles, between countries within hours. Large numbers of visitors can also strain local water, food supplies and health services.
The benefits depend on who gains. If hotels are owned overseas, much of the profit can leave the country, so locals may gain little and still bear the risks.
rejected.remember: Tourism's effect on health depends on who keeps the income and how well local resources cope with visitors.

a.q: A beach resort in a low-income country is owned by an overseas company. Why might local people gain little health benefit from it?
opts: Much of the profit may flow overseas, not to local people
Overseas owners may pay higher wages than local businesses
Resort taxes may be spent on schools rather than on clinics
Visitors may use local clinics less often than residents do
a.why: When the owner is overseas, much of the profit can leave the country, so less money funds local housing, food and health care. Higher wages would add to the benefit, not reduce it, and spending on schools still supports health.
a.clue: Think about who ends up with the resort's earnings.

b.q: In a mountain town in Nepal, trekking tourism paid for a new clinic. In peak season, visitor numbers double and the clinic fills with injured trekkers. What does this show?
opts: It both funds the clinic and strains it in peak season
It mainly harms health, as visitors crowd the clinic out
It mainly helps health, as tourism paid for the clinic
It mainly harms health by bringing new infections to town
b.why: The clinic shows the income benefit, and the peak-season crowding shows strain on a local health service, so both effects are present. Saying it mainly harms health ignores that tourism paid for the clinic, and the case says nothing about infectious disease.
b.clue: Does the case show a benefit, a cost, or both?

draft.title: Tourism and health
card: Tourism is travel for leisure, business or other reasons. It is a major global industry, and it affects the health of the people who live in the places visitors go to.
Benefits
Tourism brings income and jobs to local people. Money from tourism can pay for housing, food, schools and health care, which support health and wellbeing.
Risks
Travellers can carry infectious diseases between countries and into local communities. A large number of visitors can also strain local resources such as clean water, food and health services.
Whether tourism helps or harms health depends on how it is managed and who gains from it. Local communities can gain income and still face higher disease risk or shortages of water.
draft.remember: Tourism can improve health through income and jobs, but it can also spread disease and strain local resources.

a.q: Which is a way that tourism can harm the health of a local community?
opts: Visitors can bring infectious diseases into the community
Visitors always cause local incomes to fall
Tourism removes the need for local health services
Tourism stops diseases from moving between countries
a.why: Travellers move between countries and can carry infectious diseases into local communities. The option about falling incomes is wrong because the card says tourism brings income and jobs. Tourism does not reduce the need for health services, and it does not stop diseases moving.
a.clue: Think about what travellers can carry with them.

b.q: A small island town gains many new hotel jobs from tourism. In the dry season, hotels use so much water that households run short. What does this show?
opts: Tourism can bring income and also strain local resources
Tourism has no effect on local health
Tourism only harms health in small island towns
Tourism strains resources only when it brings no jobs
b.why: The hotel jobs are an income benefit, and the water shortage is a strain on a local resource. Both can happen at the same time. The claim that tourism only harms health is wrong because the jobs bring income that can support health.
b.clue: Look for one benefit and one problem in the same town.

a.best: Visitors can bring infectious diseases into the community

b.best: Tourism can bring income and also strain local resources

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with the qualifier 'can'. The other three are absolute or extreme claims ('always', 'removes the need', 'stops'), so a student can pick the answer without knowing the idea. The clue ('what travellers can carry with them') nearly states the answer.
The right option is the longest and the only one with 'can'. The distractors all use 'only' or 'no', so the answer stands out without any understanding of the scenario.
Both questions are very easy for Year 12 VCE. The distractors are implausible, so the questions test little beyond recognising wording from the card.
The why paraphrases a distractor as 'tourism only harms health', but the option says 'Tourism only harms health in small island towns'. The rebuttal does not match the option's actual claim.

b.q: In a mountain town in Nepal, trekking tourism paid for a new clinic. In peak season, visitor numbers double and the clinic fills with injured trekkers, so local patients wait much longer. Which statement best describes the effect of tourism on local health here?

Tourism strained the health service but did not fund it
Tourism funded a health service and did not strain it
Tourism spread infection and did not fund any services
